summary: Stevens County, WA lookout: camp in 1920, cab in 1921, 40-ft tower in 1936, removed or destroyed in 1955; only radio towers reported on the summit now.

facts.design: 10x10 ft frame cab (1921); 40 ft pole L-4 tower (1936)
facts.status_note: Tower removed or destroyed in 1955; the sources describe radio towers on the summit, not a lookout

visit.trail_note: Willhite: a four-wheel-drive road reaches the summit radio towers; access rules not stated

events.note: Lookout station established with a camp; a telephone line ran from the station to Locke (1919-20 state forester report)
10x10 ft frame cab built the year after the camp
Harold Horton named as lookout (Spokane Chronicle, September 16, 1922); earliest named lookout in the sources
Mr. Dunnigan named for 1923; 1923 photo caption calls him the lookoutman
Robert C. Stegner (Spokane Daily Chronicle); Robert Stagner in Colville Examiner
Ruth Downey named in a June 19, 1930 notice that she would be on guard
Bill Crosset of Calispel lookout (Colville Examiner, September 8, 1934)
Elmer and George Davis spent the summer at the lookout (Newport Miner, September 8, 1938); last named staff in the sources
Register says removed; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed; Forest Lookouts says Removed
Registered November 23, 2012 as US 1486, WA 386; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says removed in 1955; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed. Both kept in the story; the year is not disputed.
Spokane Daily Chronicle spells it Stegner; Colville Examiner spells it Stagner. Both spellings are in the source; the name is unresolved.

sources.title: Calispell Peak Lookout Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites Register

notes_for_editor: Spelled Calispell (register, Willhite) and Calispel (Forest Lookouts) in sources; the 1920 Spokane paper spells it Kalispell. The 1936 tower's removal year agrees in three sources; the wording differs. No specific fire is credited to this lookout in the sources read, so the story names none. Access is not stated in any source; the four-wheel-drive road is from Willhite only. Staff names rest on newspaper transcriptions on the Forest Lookouts page. No web search was possible for this run (budget used up), so no newer status was checked.
